correctness.rationale: For 0<p<1, exact graph recursion forces nondecreasing vertex depths; last depth equals height. The leaf increment equals the adjacent attachment word 10. Covariance of Markov depth increments and of overlapping two-bit indicators yields all three specified long-run covariance entries. Irreducible, aperiodic finite-state Markov transition-reward theory implies a bivariate functional CLT. The derived determinant is strictly positive throughout the interior; the unique q-root gives the sharp sign reversal. A standalone checker exhaustively verifies the rooted-tree and recursion observables and 288 finite moment comparisons; finite experiments are not treated as proof of the limit.

originality.rationale: The July 2026 motivating article studies the identical Bernoulli-tree model but proves topological one-endedness and infinite random-walk collisions. Its inspected proofs and branch-length section do not give the joint height-leaf Brownian limit, covariance matrix, or golden-ratio sign boundary. Published literature on uniform and scaled-attachment recursive trees has different parent laws. The finite-state invariance principle is standard; the model-specific covariance evaluation and sign transition are not implied by the inspected results. Targeted source/claim/alias searches identify no equivalent result; a differently formulated run-statistic theorem remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: Height and leaves are distinct natural geometric descriptors of a growing tree. Their sharp covariance sign reversal separates antagonistic from cooperative large-scale shape fluctuations in the simplest nontrivial bounded-lookback recursive-tree model. The closed-form positive-definite joint covariance and functional limit quantify effects absent from the marginal topology/collision study; this is more than a routine restatement of a finite-state CLT or a small numerical improvement.
